questions.q: Identify the error: “The criteria for selection is very strict.”
questions.why: 'Criteria' is the plural of 'criterion': 'are'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “ebullient”:
questions.why: 'Ebullient' means cheerful and full of energy; 'dejected' means low in spirits. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the one word for: “A disease regularly found among people in a particular area”
questions.why: An endemic disease is constantly present in a particular region or population. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “sporadic”:
questions.why: 'Sporadic' means occurring at irregular intervals; 'constant' means continuous. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct inversion of: “The accident was so terrible that the road remained closed for hours.”
opts: So terrible was the accident that the road remained closed for hours.
So terrible the accident was that the road remained closed for hours.
Such terrible was the accident that the road remained closed for hours.
So terrible did the accident was that the road remained closed for hours.
questions.why: 'So + adjective' in front position inverts the verb 'be' and the subject. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Change into direct speech: The patient asked the doctor whether he could go home that day.
opts: The patient said to the doctor, “Can I go home today?”
The patient said to the doctor, “Can he go home today?”
The patient said to the doctor, “Can I go home that day?”
The patient said to the doctor, “May I go home yesterday?”
questions.why: 'Could' returns to 'can', 'that day' returns to 'today', and the question order is restored. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “If he had listened to the doctor then, he ____ in hospital now.”
questions.why: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the error: “The secret must remain between you and I.”
questions.why: A preposition takes the objective case: 'between you and me'. GPSC-style practice item.
Ends in -ible: irresistible. GPSC-style practice item.
The question mark stays inside the quotes and no comma follows it. GPSC-style practice item.
